misconceptions.average-of-sides: Averaged two different one-sided limits. When they disagree, there is no limit.
misconceptions.dot-is-right-side: Used the filled dot as one side's limit.
misconceptions.dropped-denominator: Removed the bottom without dividing the top by it.
misconceptions.flipped: Put the simplified expression on the wrong side of the fraction bar.
misconceptions.hole-means-no-limit: Thought a hole at the point stops the limit. Both sides still head to the same height.
misconceptions.kept-cancelled-factor: Kept the factor that cancels and dropped the one that stays.
misconceptions.limit-is-value: Read the limit off the filled dot (the value f(a)) instead of where the graph is heading.
misconceptions.limit-needs-value: Thought a limit needs a value at the point itself. It only uses values near the point.
misconceptions.same-not-conjugate: Multiplied by the same expression instead of the conjugate (flip the sign in the middle).
misconceptions.sides-swapped: Swapped the left-hand and right-hand limits.
misconceptions.sign-slip: Lost track of the sign in the conjugate after simplifying.
misconceptions.top-is-zero: Took the limit to be 0 because the top is 0 at the point, ignoring the bottom.
misconceptions.wrong-factor: Multiplied by a factor that doesn't remove the square root.
misconceptions.wrong-root-sign: Factored with the wrong signs: a root at x = r gives the factor (x − r).
misconceptions.zero-over-zero-dne: Took 0/0 to mean no limit. It means the algebra isn't finished.
misconceptions.zero-over-zero-is-0: Took 0/0 to be 0. It's a signal to simplify, not a value.
